newsitem.title: FRANCE: My name is Bond, James Bond. These are my cars.
newsitem.headline: My name is Bond, James Bond. These are my cars.

text.p: There is a secret agent among the crowd at the Paris Motor Show and he has an entire hall devoted to his cars, weapons and women.
He is agent 007 -- Commander James Bond.
No less than 23 of the cars used in the films on Britain's famous fictional spy are displayed in a hall of some 5,000 square metres at the show, which runs from October 1 until October 13.

And its not only cars. There are helicopters, boats, tanks, a gondola and even the double-decker bus from "Live and Let Die", which ends up as a single decker bus after escaping from a police pursuit by driving under a low bridge.

There are life-size dummies depicting characters from the movies in their original costumes plus some live models -- including a lady dressed in nothing but gold paint and a G-string like the actress in the 1964 movie "Goldfinger" which featured Sean Connery as Bond.
Bond is famous for his Aston Martin DB5 sportscar but this vehicle does not make its appearance until "Goldfinger", the third Bond film.
The first movie, "Doctor No", with Connery and Ursula Andress in 1962, was graced with a Sunbeam Alpine roadster and a Chevrolet Bel-Air.
In "From Russia With Love", Bond luxuriates in a Rolls-Royce Park Ward Limousine from 1952, plus a 1950 Citroen Traction Avant 11 and a Bentley Drophead Coupe.
Georges Lazenby becomes Bond in "Her Majesty's Secret Service" with an Aston Martin DBS. In 1971 Connery returns in "Diamonds are Forever" with a Triumph Stag and a Ford Mustang.
Roger Moore played Bond in seven movies, from 1973 to 1985 and enjoyed a whole range of cars, but none of them an Aston.

Timothy Dalton, in the 1989 episode "Licence to Kill", renews the Bond-Aston tie-up and Pierce Brosnan, in "GoldenEye" in 1995, continues on the Aston road -- while adding nothing less than a Russian T-54 tank to the panoply.
All the cars and props have been made available by private collectors and the James Bond fan club.
The organisers also arranged for Mr Q, actor Desmond Llewellyn, and Miss Moneypenny, Lois Maxwell, to grace the press days.
Bond was invented by the late novelist Ian Fleming, a former Reuter correspondent
